android.extraProguardRules:
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FurlPay release hardening. Applied on top of proguard-android.txt.
#
# Shrinking and obfuscation are enabled (enableProguardInReleaseBuilds), so the
# job here is (a) keep what is reached only by reflection or JNI, and (b) remove
# what must not ship. Every keep names a dependency that is actually installed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- crash symbolication ---------------------------------------------------
# Obfuscation renames everything, which makes a production stack trace useless
# unless the line table survives and the mapping file is kept. LineNumberTable
# gives frames their line numbers back; renamesourcefileattribute collapses the
# original filenames to a single token so the source layout is NOT disclosed
# while traces stay symbolicatable against mapping.txt.
# EAS retains mapping.txt per build; upload it to the crash reporter on release.
-keepattributes SourceFile,LineNumberTable
-renamesourcefileattribute SourceFile

# Reflection, generics and Kotlin metadata all read these at runtime. Without
# them Gson-style reflective access and Kotlin's own reflection break in ways
# that only appear in a release build.
-keepattributes *Annotation*,Signature,InnerClasses,EnclosingMethod

# --- STRIP DEBUG LOGGING FROM RELEASE --------------------------------------
# The headline gap this file previously had. A wallet logs addresses, amounts,
# request ids and occasionally response bodies during development; every one of
# those reaches logcat, which any app with READ_LOGS — and anyone with adb —
# can read off the device.
#
# v/d/i are removed. w/e are DELIBERATELY KEPT: they are what a crash reporter
# and a support engineer read, and stripping them would trade a real diagnostic
# for no additional secrecy, since the app does not log secrets at those levels.
-assumenosideeffects class android.util.Log {
    public static int v(...);
    public static int d(...);
    public static int i(...);
    public static boolean isLoggable(...);
}

# React Native's own JS console bridge on the native side. Same reasoning.
-assumenosideeffects class com.facebook.common.logging.FLog {
    public static void v(...);
    public static void d(...);
    public static void i(...);
}

# --- React Native core -----------------------------------------------------
# The bridge resolves native modules and view managers BY NAME at runtime, so
# R8 cannot see the references. DoNotStrip is RN's own marker for exactly this.
-keep,includedescriptorclasses class com.facebook.react.turbomodule.** { *; }
-keepclassmembers class * { @com.facebook.proguard.annotations.DoNotStrip *; }
-keepclassmembers class * { @com.facebook.react.uimanager.annotations.ReactProp <methods>; }
-keepclassmembers class * { @com.facebook.react.bridge.ReactMethod <methods>; }
# JNI entry points: a renamed method is a method the native side cannot find.
-keepclasseswithmembernames class * { native <methods>; }

# --- Hermes ----------------------------------------------------------------
# The engine is loaded through JNI; its facade classes are never referenced
# from Java code R8 can see.
-keep class com.facebook.hermes.unicode.** { *; }
-keep class com.facebook.jni.** { *; }

# --- Expo modules ----------------------------------------------------------
# expo-modules-core discovers modules reflectively from the generated package
# list. Renaming them breaks every Expo native module at once.
-keep class expo.modules.** { *; }
-keep class * extends expo.modules.kotlin.modules.Module { *; }

# --- react-native-passkey (^3.5.0) ------------------------------------------
# Bridges to AndroidX Credential Manager, which resolves request/response types
# reflectively across a process boundary.
-keep class com.reactnativepasskey.** { *; }
-keep class androidx.credentials.** { *; }
-keep class com.google.android.gms.fido.** { *; }

# --- @maplibre/maplibre-react-native (^10.4.2) ------------------------------
# The renderer is native (C++/JNI) and calls back into these classes by name.
-keep class org.maplibre.** { *; }
-keep class com.maplibre.** { *; }
-dontwarn org.maplibre.**

# --- expo-sqlite (~15.2.14) -------------------------------------------------
# JNI bindings into the bundled SQLite.
-keep class expo.modules.sqlite.** { *; }

# --- @react-native-async-storage/async-storage (2.1.2) ----------------------
# Required by @walletconnect/react-native-compat for relay session storage.
-keep class com.reactnativecommunity.asyncstorage.** { *; }

# --- @react-native-community/netinfo (11.4.1) -------------------------------
-keep class com.reactnativecommunity.netinfo.** { *; }

# --- react-native-svg (15.11.2) ---------------------------------------------
# View managers are resolved by name from JS.
-keep public class com.horcrux.svg.** { *; }

# --- react-native-screens (~4.11.1) -----------------------------------------
-keep class com.swmansion.rnscreens.** { *; }

# --- OkHttp / Okio ----------------------------------------------------------
# RN's networking stack. These -dontwarn entries suppress warnings about
# optional compile-time-only references (Conscrypt, Animal Sniffer, BouncyCastle)
# that are genuinely absent at runtime; without them R8 fails the build on
# classes nothing actually calls.
-dontwarn okhttp3.**
-dontwarn okio.**
-dontwarn org.conscrypt.**
-dontwarn org.bouncycastle.**
-dontwarn org.openjsse.**
-dontwarn javax.annotation.**
-dontwarn org.codehaus.mojo.animal_sniffer.*

# --- Kotlin coroutines ------------------------------------------------------
# Used by every Expo Kotlin module. The service loader entry is read by name.
-keepclassmembers class kotlinx.coroutines.** { volatile <fields>; }
-dontwarn kotlinx.coroutines.**

# --- JNA / desktop-only AWT ------------------------------------------------
# R8 fails the release build with:
#   Missing class java.awt.Component
#     (referenced from: long com.sun.jna.Native.getWindowHandle0(java.awt.Component))
#
# JNA arrives transitively and carries a desktop code path that takes an AWT
# component to get a native window handle. java.awt does not exist on Android
# and that method is unreachable here, so the reference is genuinely dead — the
# warning is R8 being correct about a class it cannot resolve, not a real
# missing dependency.
#
# -dontwarn (NOT -keep): keeping it would be impossible (the class does not
# exist) and suppressing the warning is exactly what the Android Gradle plugin
# generates into missing_rules.txt for this case. Scoped to the single class R8
# named rather than the whole java.awt package, so a future genuinely-missing
# AWT reference still fails the build instead of being silently swallowed.
-dontwarn java.awt.Component
